<description>
**Problem:** `CheckBlockDataAvailability` checks whether the upper block has any requested bit. `GetFirstBlock` requires every requested bit, so a partial match can reach its assertion. At genesis, the existing undo exception can reject an undo-only request or accept a request with missing block data. It also misses ranges containing only genesis.

**Fix:** Require every requested bit on each block in the range, except that genesis needs no undo data. An empty mask now succeeds for a valid range because it requests no bits. Both index-startup calls supply nonempty masks.
</description>

<commits>
bb84dda2fe test: characterize block data availability masks

Record the availability results for genesis and partially available blocks before fixing the mask checks.
Use `Assert` for the full-mask precondition in `GetFirstBlock` so the unit test can observe which availability requests violate it.

6f4519c466 blockstorage: reject missing data at the lower block

The genesis undo exception accepts any matching requested flag, so `BLOCK_OPT_WITNESS` can hide missing block data at genesis.
Check the lower block for missing requested bits before walking the range, exempting only genesis undo data.
When both endpoints are the same pruned block with only undo data, a request for block data and undo data now returns `false` before reaching the walker assertion.
Assert the existing `cs_main` requirement on entry so it also covers the early returns.

dbd2c96276 blockstorage: honor the undo exception for genesis-only ranges

When the endpoints coincide, checking the lower block covers the whole range.
Return early in that case so neither the upper block check nor `GetFirstBlock` requires undo data from genesis.
This also accepts an empty mask on a single-block range because it requests no bits.

08ec1a6685 blockstorage: reject partial upper-block matches before GetFirstBlock

`GetFirstBlock` requires every requested bit on its starting block.
Reject an upper block missing any of those bits before calling the walker.
This also accepts an empty mask on a multi-block range because it requests no bits.

41851dc3c3 blockstorage: honor undo-only requests down to genesis

The old genesis branch rejected undo-only requests because it looked for a matching flag after removing the only requested bit.
Genesis has already passed the lower block check.
If the walk stops at its child because genesis lacks undo data, the whole range is available.
Every other lower block has already passed the full mask check, so the walk cannot stop at its child.
</commits>
